items.contentMarkdown:
Source: BBC Learning English — 6 Minute English (selected episode)
URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/features/6-minute-english/ep-211007

Listening focus (choose one):
- 1-minute focus: Listen to identify the single sentence that defines what a sensor does.
- 2-minute focus: Listen for two examples of sensors mentioned and the signals they measure (e.g., light, position).
- 4-minute focus: Listen for how sensors help a mechatronics system make decisions and one advantage given.

Comprehension & reflection questions (use first 2 for very short activities; first 4 for standard; all 6 for extended):
1) What is the main purpose of a sensor in a machine? (simple factual)
2) Name one example of a sensor mentioned and what it detects. (simple factual)
3) How does a sensor send information to other parts of a system? (short inference)
4) Why is reliable sensor data important for a robot or automated machine? (short explanation)
5) Think of one sensor a recent mechatronics project might need. How would it improve the system? (application)
6) Reflect: In your future work, how would you test sensor accuracy before assembly? Describe two checks. (planning/reflection)

Phrase-capture instruction:
While listening, write down one short phrase (3–5 words) that describes what a sensor measures or does in the recording (do not use a transcript). Try to copy the phrase exactly as you hear it.

items.titleEnglish: 6 Minute English — Actuators (small motors and actuators)
items.contentMarkdown:
Source: BBC Learning English — 6 Minute English (selected episode)
URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/learningenglish/features/6-minute-english_2025/ep-250918

Listening focus (choose one):
- 1-minute focus: Listen for a clear phrase that explains what an actuator does.
- 2-minute focus: Listen for two types of actuators or motors mentioned and one example use for each.
- 4-minute focus: Listen for advantages and limitations of a small actuator in precision tasks.

Comprehension & reflection questions (use first 2 for very short activities; first 4 for standard; all 6 for extended):
1) What does an actuator do in a machine? (simple factual)
2) Give one example of where a small actuator might be used. (simple factual)
3) How is an actuator different from a sensor? (comparison)
4) What is one limitation of using a small actuator in heavy tasks? (short inference)
5) Suggest a mechatronics design where choosing the right actuator changes performance. Explain briefly. (application)
6) Reflect: Describe a test you would run to check an actuator's response time and repeatability. (planning/reflection)

Phrase-capture instruction:
Listen and write one short phrase (2–4 words) that describes an action an actuator performs in the audio. Do not use a transcript.

5) Apply: For a line-following robot, what controller inputs and outputs are essential? List two of each. (application)
6) Reflect: How would you plan an update to controller code without disrupting a running system in a lab test? (planning/reflection)

While listening, note one short technical phrase (2–5 words) that describes a controller’s role. Copy it exactly as heard.

Source: BBC Learning English — 6 Minute English (selected episode)

Listening focus (choose one):
- 1-minute focus: Listen for the sentence that explains why components must 'talk' to each other.
- 2-minute focus: Listen for two communication methods or protocols mentioned (e.g., wired, wireless, serial).
- 4-minute focus: Listen for one challenge in system integration and a suggested way to test communication reliability.

Comprehension & reflection questions (use first 2 for very short activities; first 4 for standard; all 6 for extended):
1) Why is communication between components important? (simple factual)
2) Name one method devices use to communicate mentioned in the audio. (simple factual)
3) What is one common problem when parts do not communicate properly? (short inference)
4) How can testing help find communication errors before full deployment? (short explanation)
5) Apply: For a distributed sensor network, which test would you run first to check data flow? Explain briefly. (application)
6) Reflect: Describe how you would document interface requirements when you hand over a module to another engineer. (planning/reflection)

Phrase-capture instruction:
During the listening, write down one short phrase (3–6 words) that describes how components communicate or a testing method mentioned.
